purpose: Reference compositions used to validate the starting research profile contract. They are examples and balance seeds, not playable-species tech trees. Species/start definitions may select different fragment combinations when historically justified.

profiles.description: Reference for the established human-like 2050 direction: mature homeworld science, substantial orbital activity, permanent off-world settlement, carbon-centered water-solvent biology, but no mature practical fusion or FTL.
profiles.historical_notes: The reference profile deliberately leaves fusion as Investigable and does not seed FTL hypotheses. Carbon-water biology is explicit historical context, not a universal biology assumption.

profiles.description: Reference for a naturally or historically synthetic civilization that reaches a comparable early-space era through a machine-oriented scientific history.
profiles.historical_notes: This profile begins with machine cognition as an existing civilization fact but does not claim the civilization researched the human Synthetic Cognition path.

profiles.description: Reference for a carbon-water metabolic high-gravity civilization with strong medicine/materials needs and an otherwise comparable early-space scientific foundation.
profiles.historical_notes: High-gravity pressure can expose several solutions, but the profile chooses none of them in advance.

profiles.description: Reference for a carbon-water metabolic civilization whose settlement history has already produced serious low-gravity medical/developmental questions.
profiles.historical_notes: Low-gravity experience changes the starting research horizon through pressure and competence rather than a species-specific tree.

profiles.description: Reference for a carbon-water civilization native to a high-pressure liquid environment with a comparable early-space scientific foundation.
profiles.historical_notes: Liquid-medium and pressure conditions shape the starting horizon without prescribing a separate future tree or granting advanced ocean habitats.
